bottom_line: Stocks got hammered this week because the AI trade that pushed the market up all year is now falling apart. At the same time the Fed, the people who set interest rates, is talking about raising rates to fight inflation instead of cutting them to help.

stories.title: The AI stock rout hits everything
stories.real: The S&P 500 and the Dow closed in a correction, which means a big drop from their recent highs. The Nasdaq wiped out all its gains for 2026, and the Nasdaq 100 is close to a bear market, an even deeper drop. Chip stocks had their worst week since 2001. AI companies are worth so much that when they fall, the whole market falls with them. Anthropic's shares also dropped after its first day of public trading, which added to the slide.

stories.title: Nvidia's rough stretch gets worse
stories.real: Nvidia stock fell 14% and finished its longest run of weekly losses since the 2008 financial crisis. It used to be the most valuable company in the world and now ranks third, behind Apple and Microsoft. An SEC accounting probe (the SEC is the government's stock-market cop) is adding to the pressure. Its former CEO Jensen Huang is set to testify publicly before a Senate panel after criticism over his involvement with a suspected Chinese spy. Big options traders are also betting that chip stocks have further to fall.
stories.you: One company this big moving this much can drag down the funds most people own, even if you never bought Nvidia yourself.

stories.title: The Fed is leaning toward raising rates
stories.real: Fed officials, including Governor Lisa Cook, are saying inflation is still too high and rate hikes are needed. They mostly disagree about how fast to go, and some are floating a half-point hike at the Dec. 9 meeting. Some Fed officials are also warning that the AI boom itself could push prices up. Trump is attacking the Fed for keeping rates high, but it is focused on inflation, not on rescuing the stock market.
stories.you: Higher rates usually mean more expensive credit cards, car loans and mortgages, though savings accounts can pay a bit more.

stories.title: Trump threatens tax on overseas data centers
stories.real: After a summit in China with Xi and Putin, Trump said he would stop US companies from building AI data centers in other countries and threatened a 'tremendous tax.' He gave few details, and even people on his own team were hearing about it for the first time. Meanwhile, building data centers in the US already costs 13% more this year because there isn't enough powered land or enough workers.
stories.you: Big tech companies face more uncertainty and higher costs, and that is part of why their stocks are under pressure right now.

stories.real: Polls show Americans feel bad about the economy and are worried about costs. One analysis says the economy is doing better than people think, just not for everyone.
stories.you: If your budget feels tight even though the headlines say the economy is fine, you're not imagining it. Rising prices are the main worry.
